parts.note: Victoria was the British queen who reigned through most of the nineteenth century
plum means choice or excellent, as in a plum job

explanation.surface: A royal favourite in the fruit bowl.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a well-known variety of English plum, red and sweet, so it is a type of fruit.

indicators.note: first tells us the green piece comes ahead of the rest, though the clue mentions it last

parts.note: vert is green in heraldry
a go is a turn, as in a board game

explanation.surface: Someone feeling dizzy and turning green.
explanation.definitionFit: Vertigo is a spinning sensation, a kind of giddiness; the question mark flags the less common medical sense.

clue.text: Before start of Easter, dispenser's short shift

indicators.note: Before places the trimmed pharmacist ahead of the Easter letter
short asks us to drop the final letter of the pharmacist word

parts.note: a chemist dispenses medicines in Britain

indicators.note: start of takes just the opening letter of the word Easter

explanation.surface: A pharmacist working a reduced shift before the Easter holiday.
explanation.definitionFit: A shift is a loose straight dress or slip, which is exactly what this garment is.

indicators.note: managed suggests the letters of the two words are handled and rearranged

explanation.surface: An honest person who managed to come out on top.
explanation.walkthrough: In betting, money placed 'to win' only pays if the horse finishes first, which is the same as a bet placed on the nose.
explanation.definitionFit: A bet on the nose is a racing idiom for a wager that pays only if the horse finishes first.

indicators.note: having lost tells us one letter is taken away from the freebooter word

parts.note: a freebooter is a pirate
P is the standard abbreviation for power in physics

explanation.surface: A pirate in a rage after losing his strength.
explanation.definitionFit: Irate is a direct synonym of furious, meaning very angry.

parts.note: prim means prudish and strait-laced
ate is the past tense of eat, so it means dined

explanation.surface: A prudish senior churchman who had dinner.
explanation.definitionFit: A primate is the title of the chief bishop of a province, such as the Archbishop of Canterbury.

clue.text: Social climber put out, interrupted by celebrity

indicators.note: interrupted by says the shuffled letters are broken open by another word
out signals the letters of put are thrown out of order

parts.note: a star is a celebrity

explanation.surface: An ambitious newcomer annoyed because a famous person cut in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' looks like part of 'put out' meaning annoyed, but it is the anagram signal; 'interrupted by' then breaks the shuffled letters open.
explanation.definitionFit: An upstart is someone who has risen suddenly in status and behaves arrogantly, a pushy social climber.

clue.text: Family doctor elected to cut mass of thick hair, a vivid colour

indicators.note: to cut means the following pieces slice into the mop of hair

parts.note: a shock is a thick mop of hair
kin are family
GP, general practitioner, is a family doctor in Britain
in means elected, as a party voted in

explanation.surface: A family doctor gets voted in to trim someone's bushy hair, which is brightly coloured.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Family doctor' reads as one idea, but it splits into two pieces; 'to cut' sends them, with the word for elected, into the mop of hair between its last two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a bright intense pink made famous by the designer Schiaparelli, so it is a vivid hue.

indicators.note: mostly asks for all but the last letter of the word meaning stiff

parts.note: hard means stiff or rigid
a vest is a British undershirt

explanation.surface: A rigid piece of underwear.
explanation.definitionFit: Produce here is a noun, the crops gathered in, which is what a farmer's yield or crop gathering means.

parts.note: tissue is a fine, thin gauzy cloth

explanation.surface: A thin, see-through material being talked about.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase at issue is an idiom for the matter being debated or in question.

parts.note: an emerald is a precious stone
green means fresh or new, as in green vegetables or a green recruit

explanation.surface: A gem that brings a new tint.
explanation.definitionFit: This bright green shade is named for the gemstone, so it is a colour.

clue.text: Copper is at home with English style of cooking

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
in means at home

explanation.surface: A policeman at home with English food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' suggests a policeman, but it is the metal, symbol CU.
explanation.definitionFit: Cuisine is a characteristic manner of preparing food, French cuisine for instance.

clue.text: Revolving handle getting a note to emerge

indicators.note: Revolving says the word for handle is turned round and read backwards

parts.note: a handle is slang for a name
te is the seventh note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A rotating door handle produces a sound as it opens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolving' turns NAME into EMAN; 'handle' is not a knob but a name.
explanation.definitionFit: To emanate is to issue or flow out from a source, which is to come forth or appear.

parts.note: in on means party to, or aware of, a secret

indicators.note: lead takes the opening letter of the football club name

explanation.surface: Manchester United know about Everton's advantage in the match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'United' looks like the football club rival of Everton; it is the definition. Everton is an English football team.
explanation.definitionFit: In one means together as a single unit, so united or combined.

clue.text: Band of gold artist put round part of the trunk

indicators.note: put round tells us the gold and artist pieces go either side of the body part

parts.note: or is gold in heraldry
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist
the chest is part of the torso, the body's trunk

explanation.surface: A gold-loving artist wraps something round a tree trunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trunk' suggests a tree but means the human torso.
explanation.definitionFit: An orchestra is a large group of musicians, a band in the broad sense.

indicators.note: in a down clue on to places the prisoners above the coaching word

parts.note: cons is short for convicts, prisoners
to train is to coach

explanation.surface: Inmates being pushed onto a bus.
explanation.definitionFit: To constrain is to compel or oblige, which is to force someone.

clue.text: Start to back small new broker

parts.note: go means start, as in ready, steady, go
to back a horse is to bet on it
wee is Scottish for small

explanation.surface: Beginning to support a small new stockbroker.
explanation.definitionFit: A go-between is an intermediary who negotiates between parties, which is what a broker does.

clue.text: Number giving support to revolutionary Labour prime minister

indicators.note: in a down clue a piece giving support sits underneath the other
revolutionary tells us the party abbreviation is turned round

parts.note: Lab is the abbreviation for the British Labour Party
four is a number

explanation.surface: A figure backing a radical Labour premier.
explanation.walkthrough: Labour is a British political party, abbreviated in print; 'revolutionary' turns that abbreviation round, and in a down clue the number sits beneath it as support.
explanation.definitionFit: Arthur Balfour was the Conservative British prime minister from 1902 to 1905.

clue.text: A classic article on timber trees

indicators.note: in a down clue on places the article above the trees

parts.note: the is the definite article
oaks are trees grown for timber

explanation.surface: A classic piece of writing about forestry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A classic' suggests a book, but it is one of the five British Classics, the great flat horse races; the Oaks is run at Epsom for fillies.
explanation.definitionFit: The Oaks is one of Britain's five Classic flat races, a race for three-year-old fillies at Epsom.

parts.note: a daily is a British term for a cleaning lady, also called a char

indicators.note: primarily picks out the first letter of delivery

explanation.surface: Beetroot brought every day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Daily' reads as an adjective about deliveries; in British usage it is a noun, a cleaner, also a char.
explanation.definitionFit: Chard is a leafy vegetable of the beet family, also called Swiss chard.

definitions.meaning: a dated British exclamation meaning splendid
Havana is the chief city of Cuba, seat of its government

explanation.definitionFit: The word means first-rate in old slang and also a seat of government, as Havana is.

parts.note: to attach is to join or fasten

explanation.surface: An instruction to link up with a European envoy.
explanation.definitionFit: An attache is an embassy official, a junior member of a diplomatic staff.

clue.text: Ailment comes from cool headland, blowing cold and hot

indicators.note: blowing is used in the sense of losing or squandering, so these letters go

parts.note: chill means cool
C is the abbreviation for cold on taps
H is the abbreviation for hot on taps
ness is a headland, as in Loch Ness or Dungeness

explanation.surface: Someone falls sick on a windswept cape where the weather swings between cold and hot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blowing' sounds like the wind on the headland, but it means squandering: CHILLNESS loses its C and H.
explanation.definitionFit: Illness is a straightforward synonym for an ailment or sickness.

clue.text: Conductor turned up in Kuwait, lost

indicators.note: turned up says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A maestro surfaced, having gone missing in the Gulf.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'turned up' means read upwards; 'in' points to the letters ITLOS inside the phrase, which reverse.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Georg Solti was a celebrated Hungarian-British orchestral conductor.

parts.note: read better as a noun, a gambler, so this is someone who advises people who bet

explanation.definitionFit: A tipster sells predictions on races to punters, advice for someone placing bets.

clue.text: Cocky type rounded hill, was almost captured

indicators.note: captured says the hill holds the shortened word inside it

parts.note: a knoll is a small rounded hill

indicators.note: almost asks for all but the last letter of was

explanation.surface: An arrogant person rounded up a hill and was nearly caught.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rounded hill' looks like a description but is a single word; 'almost' drops the last letter of 'was', and 'captured' places what is left near the end of the hill word.
explanation.definitionFit: A know-all is a person who acts as if they know everything, a conceited cocky sort.

indicators.note: in places the numeral letter inside the rearranged word
amended suggests the letters of cartel are altered and rearranged

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A single member of a price-fixing group changed a contract term.
explanation.walkthrough: 'amended' turns CARTEL into ARTCLE, and 'in' puts I between T and C.
explanation.definitionFit: An article is a separate clause or section of a legal document, treaty or contract.

clue.text: Old German, down delivering a pigment

parts.note: Prussia was a former German state, so a Prussian is an old-style German
blue means depressed or down

explanation.surface: A dejected German of the old school produces some paint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'down' looks like feathers or a direction; here it means sad.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a deep blue ferrocyanide pigment used in paints and blueprints.
